The '''2015–16 Scottish Premiership''' (known as the [[Ladbrokes|Ladbrokes Premiership]] for sponsorship reasons) was the third season of the [[Scottish Premiership]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]]. The season began on 1 August 2015.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/aberdeen/318980-scottish-premiership-201516-campaign-set-for-start-on-august-1/ | title=Scottish Premiership 2015/16 campaign set for start on August 1 | publisher=STV | date=30 April 2015 | access-date=30 April 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518091751/http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/aberdeen/318980-scottish-premiership-201516-campaign-set-for-start-on-august-1/ | archive-date=18 May 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Celtic were the defending champions.

Twelve teams contested the league: [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

== Tournament format and regulations ==

=== Basic ===
In the initial phase of the season, the 12 teams will play a round-robin tournament whereby each team plays each one of the other teams three times. After 33 games, the league splits into two sections of six teams, with each team playing each other in that section. The league attempts to balance the fixture list so that teams in the same section play each other twice at home and twice away, but sometimes this is impossible. A total of 228 matches will be played, with 38 matches played by each team.

=== Promotion and relegation ===
Heart of Midlothian were promoted as 2014–15 Scottish Championship winners. On 2 May, bottom club Dundee United were defeated 2–1 away to their city rivals Dundee, a defeat which confined them to relegation of the [[Scottish Championship|Championship]]. Craig Wighton, a local Dundee fan, scored the winning goal in the 92nd minute of the game. The champion of that league will be promoted to the Premiership for the 2016–17 season. The team that finishes 11th in the Premiership will play the winner of the Championship playoffs (teams that finish 2nd, 3rd and 4th in the Championship) in two playoff games, with the winner securing a Premiership spot for the 2016–17 season.

==Premiership play-offs==
The quarter-finals were contested between the 3rd and 4th placed teams in the [[2015–16 Scottish Championship|Scottish Championship]]; [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]]. Hibernian, the winners, advanced to the semi-finals to face the 2nd placed team in the Championship; [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]. Falkirk, the winners, advanced to the final to play-off against the 11th placed team in the Premiership,  [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], with the winners securing a place in the [[2016–17 Scottish Premiership]].
